_exec_summary.SummaryText:
The City of Fremont, Nebraska (City) contracted with HDR Engineering, Inc. (HDR) to assess the Process Safety Management Program (PSM)/Risk Management Program (RMP) at its Biogas Conditioning System (BCS) within the Fremont Wastewater Treatment Plant. Because the BCS stores methane in an amount that exceeds regulatory threshold limits, the City is required to prepare a Program Level 3 RMP/PSM in compliance with 40 CFR Part 68.
The BCS produces biogas from its anaerobic lagoons and digesters to treat approximately 5-million gallons of wastewater per day. The BCS takes the methane produced from the biogas and conditions it for natural gas use. The amount of biogas produced and stored at the BCS exceeds the EPA and OSHA 10,000-pound regulatory thresholds.
HDRs objective was to evaluate the RMP procedures, documentation, and practices being used at the BCS and determine if the appropriate elements of process safety are implemented at the WWTP. The assessment included a review of the facilitys management system and a review of each RMP program element (files/sections). EPAs 40 CFR Part 68  Chemical Accident Prevention Provisions audit checklist was used as the assessment guide (May 18, 2021). To better assess employee awareness of the safety procedures, program rules and emergency assignments, two persons whose job duties involved the biogas system were interviewed: Korey Perry, Wastewater Treatment Facility Mechanic II with 14 years relevant experience, and Dylan Riecken, Instrument Control Technician with 7 years relevant experience. As a record of the event, HDR prepared this report to present the assessment findings and observations, and associated recommendations. City personnel participating in the assessment were: Keith Kontor, Wastewater Superintendent with 20 years experience at the plant, Scott Seelhoff, Assistant Wastewater Superintendent with 11 years experience at the plant, and Zach Homolka, Fremont Environmental Coordinator with approximately 2 years

 experience at the City of Fremont. The assessment (interviews, site visit and walk through, document review) was performed on December 12, 2024.
1.0 Management System {40 CFR 68.15}
The owner or operator of a stationary source with processes subject to Program 2 or Program 3 shall develop a management system to oversee the implementation of the risk management program elements.
Findings
The BCS Superintendent and Assistant Superintendent have a general emergency procedure document maintained by the City of Fremont in electronic files. A specified Emergency Action Plan (EAP) for the Fremont WWTP is in progress.
Recommendations
Store the EAP, Standard Operating Procedure documents (SOP), and Organization Chart in one electronic file and one physical file in the Administration Building to be available to all facility employees.
2.0 Hazard Assessment {40 CFR 68 Subpart B} / Risk Management Plan {40 CFR 68}
The owner or operator of a stationary source with a chemical amount greater than a threshold quantity shall prepare worst-case and alternate-case release scenarios and a five-year accident history. Re-submit a Risk Management Plan to EPA every five years.
Findings
The facility conducted an off-site consequence analysis and will report this information toEPA in the 2024 RMP ESubmit.
Recommendations
Contact neighboring properties about potential releases of methane and emergencyresponse by contacting the City of Fremont Emergency Management Office.
3.0 Process Safety Information (PSI) {40 CFR 68.65  29 CFR 1910.119(d)}
Maintain complete and accurate information on the process technology, process equipment, hazardous characteristics, and physical properties of the regulated chemical.
Findings
The BCS operating and maintenance manual is located in the Electrical/MaintenanceBuilding. Additional copies are available electronically online.
Recommendations
Update paper copies of Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and SOPs as changes occur.
Establish a record of employees who

have been trained on the manual and update therecord after refresher trainings.
4.0 Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) {40 CFR 68.67  29 CFR 1910.119(e)}
Identify and assess process hazards for the regulated process and take action to manage risk. The process hazard analyses must be updated at least every five years and retained for the life of the process.
Findings
The Process Safety Information (PSI) section of the PHA document, which provides awritten description of the chemical characteristics, the process technology, and theprocess equipment, is adequate.
The BCS is equipped with automatic shut off system that will not interfere with theWWTPs entire water treatment system.
The anerobic lagoons can store several weeks worth of biogas production in case of a BCSshut down.
The WWTPs rural location allows for the rural and City of Fremont Fire Departments tocome to the plant, depending on availability.
Recommendations
Coordinate with the City of Fremont Emergency Management Office to get hazmat firedepartment personnel onsite in case of hazmat emergency, as rural fire rescue team isnot hazmat trained.

5.0 Standard Operating Procedures {40 CFR 68.69  29 CFR 1910.119(f)}
Written Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) must provide clear instructions for safely conducting activities involving the regulated process and must also be consistent with the PSI. The SOPs must include steps for each operating phase, operating limits, safety and health considerations and safety systems and their functions. SOPs must also be available to implement safe work practices to provide for special circumstances such as lockout/tagout, confined space entry, and line break.
Findings
Directions and procedures regarding safety and health considerations and exposure control measures were provided in the latest version of the SOPs.
SOPs were available in paper copy throughout the BCS.
Recommen

dations
Update annually and make review readily available online and update paper copies aswell.
Complete annual methane and SOP/EAP updates with employees.
6.0 Training {40 CFR 68.71  29 CFR 1910.119(g)}
Employees involved with operation of the regulated process must be provided process overview and standard operating procedure training. Training must also emphasize specific safety and health hazards, emergency operations, and safe work practices. Documented refresher training is required at least every three years.
Findings
The City of Fremont Safety Director conducts an annual Safe Equipment Workshop for allemployees.
Recommendations
Include methane SOP/EAP within this workshop and document training logs.
Conduct methane release drills to practice evacuation procedures annually.
Conduct fire and sever weather drills annually.
7.0 Mechanical Integrity {40 CFR 68.73  29 CFR 1910.119(j)}
A mechanical integrity program must include identifying and categorizing equipment and instrumentation, inspections and tests and their frequency; maintenance procedures; training of maintenance personnel; criteria for acceptable test results; documentation of test and inspection results; and documentation of manufacturer recommendations for equipment and instrumentation.
Findings
The Work Order Database (PM System) addresses the elements of maintenance,inspection, cleaning, replacement and testing of the BCS.
Maintenance keeps little stock of extra equipment onsite. Personnel will acquirenecessary equipment at local stores, e.g. Menards.
Documentation and records on maintenance training is kept in electronic file foldersavailable to all employees.
Recommendations
None.
8.0 Program Audits {40 CFR 68.79  29 CFR 1910.119(o)}
Evaluate compliance with process safety requirements at least every three years.
Findings
The 2024 initial program assessment is the first conducted.RecommendationsKeep 2024 PHA worksheet in electronic file folders along with other PHAdocumentation.

9.0 Incident Investigation {40 CFR 68.81  29 CFR 1910.119(m)}
Investigate as soon as possible (but no later than 48 hours after) incidents which did result or could have resulted in catastrophic release of regulated chemicals.
Findings
No incidents have occurred at the BCS that have resulted in public impact.
Recommendations
Continue training personnel on the SOPs and involve staff with their preparation and revision.
Notify personnel of incidents after their occurrence and hold open discussions for staff post incident.
10.0 Emergency Planning and Response {40 CFR 68.90  29 CFR 1910.119(n)}
Develop and implement an emergency action plan. The emergency action plan must include procedures for handling small releases.
Findings
The EAP for incidents involving methane (incidental release, a significant release, and an uncontrolled release) and when the employees will contact the City of Fremont Emergency Management Office is in good order.
Recommendations
Verify the call list in the EAP is updated annually.
Copies of the EAP documents at operation and maintenance locations should contain thelatest updates.
Install a windsock or flag for recognition of wind direction during potential methanereleases.
Add additional signage or a fence at lagoon entrance to clearly indicate hazard area.
